quote: I know you do not make the laws, but I also know that you are the wives and mothers, the sisters and daughters of those who do; and if you really suppose you can do nothing to overthrow slavery, you are greatly mistaken.
source: Angelina Grimké, Appeal to the Christian Women of the South, answering why appeal to women, p. 16 (American Anti-Slavery Society, 1836)
note: Corrected: in the 1836 pamphlet the sentence begins To this I reply, and the quotation starts at the clause that follows, every word in order. The page is added: the passage stands on page 16, answering the objection that women make no laws and have no legislative power.

evidence.where: the 1836 American Anti-Slavery Society pamphlet, full page text of the Internet Archive scan, read directly; corroborated by the Teaching American History transcription
evidence.edition: Appeal to the Christian Women of the South, revised and corrected (American Anti-Slavery Society, New York, 1836)
evidence.locator: p. 16, the paragraph answering why appeal to women, immediately before the four things I will name

reason: The wording is exact as printed in 1836, but the quotation is lifted from the middle of a sentence that opens To this I reply, so the cut is disclosed. Page 16 is fixed by the printed 17 falling a few words later in the scan. Angelina is a different person from Sarah Moore Grimké, who stands at one for the year.
